meta.titre: Environmental Degradation and Pollution: kinds, causes, effects and control
meta.sous_theme: Degradation, conservation and the four kinds of pollution

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: After a heavy storm in Douala, gutters blocked by plastic bottles and bags make the streets flood and leave dirty water in front of the shops. In villages near the forest, farmers cut and burn trees to open new fields, and after a few seasons the tired soil gives poor harvests. These scenes show two linked problems: the damage done to our surroundings and the pollution of air, water and soil. The GCE returns to them nearly every year, asking you to explain key terms and then to give causes, effects and remedies.

items: The environment is everything around us: air, water, soil, plants, animals and the things people build.
Natural resources, such as forests, rivers and minerals, are gifts of nature that people use.
Waste is any material that people throw away because they no longer need it.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Environmental degradation | The gradual damage of the environment, when resources are used up faster than nature can renew them or when habitats are destroyed |
| Environmental conservation | The careful use, protection and management of natural resources so that they last for present and future generations |
| Deforestation | The cutting down or clearing of forests without replacing the trees |
| Afforestation / reforestation | Planting trees where there were none / replanting where a forest was cut |
| Pollution | The release of harmful substances or energy into air, water or soil, so that people, animals and plants are harmed |
| Desertification | The spread of dry, desert-like conditions into land that was once fertile |

### Kinds of pollution

| Kind | Common sources | Typical effects |
|---|---|---|
| Air | Smoke from vehicles, factories, bush fires and burning rubbish | Breathing diseases, acid rain, a warmer climate |
| Water | Sewage, household waste, chemicals from farms, factories and mining, oil spills | Waterborne diseases such as cholera and typhoid, death of fish, shortage of safe drinking water |
| Soil | Plastic and chemical waste, too many chemicals on farms | Poor crops, harm to useful living things in the soil |
| Noise | Loud engines, horns, generators and music | Hearing loss, stress, poor concentration at school |

### Causes of degradation
Logging, clearing land for farms, cutting trees for firewood and charcoal, bush burning, overgrazing, poaching and overfishing, careless mining, and growing towns without proper waste disposal. Poverty and fast population growth add pressure on resources.

### Effects
Soil erosion, floods and landslides, loss of wildlife, changes in rainfall and temperature, spreading deserts, disease, and loss of income for farmers and fishermen.

### Control and conservation
Laws against illegal logging and dumping, environmental education, tree planting, sorting and recycling waste, proper sewage systems, cleaner sources of energy, and community clean-up campaigns. World Environment Day, celebrated on 5 June, reminds everyone of this duty.

variantes.nom: Questions that say 'what do you understand by'
variantes.quand_utiliser: When two terms must be explained for about six marks
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give each term the same treatment: a precise meaning, a short explanation of what happens, and a short example. For degradation you could mention soil losing its fertility after the forest is cleared. For conservation you could mention a protected forest where cutting is controlled.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question uses these three words or one of them
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use three clear headings in your answer. Do not mix them: a cause explains why the damage starts, an effect is what follows, and a remedy is what people do to stop or repair the damage. Write one developed sentence for each point.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a short case is described and the kind must be named
variantes.contenu_markdown: Look at where the harmful thing ends up. Smoke or gas in the air is air pollution; sewage or oil in a stream is water pollution; plastic or chemicals in the ground is soil pollution; unwanted loud sound is noise pollution.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: (a) Explain what is meant by water pollution. (b) Outline three ways in which the people of a town can reduce the pollution of the river that flows through it. [8 marks]

etapes.justification: 'Explain' needs a meaning with a short development. 'Outline' needs several points, each with a brief reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) meaning of water pollution; (b) three ways to reduce it

etapes.action: Write the meaning of water pollution.
etapes.justification: Name the thing, say what enters the water and what harm follows.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Water pollution is the addition of harmful substances, such as waste, sewage or chemicals, to rivers, lakes or the sea, so that the water becomes unsafe for people and living things.

etapes.justification: Each way should act on a different source of the pollution.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Proper waste disposal; treatment of sewage and factory waste; education and fines.

etapes.action: Give a reason for each way.
etapes.justification: The reason shows that you understand how the action protects the river.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Bins and refuse collection stop waste from being thrown into the river; treated sewage carries no germs or poisons; fines and campaigns change behaviour.

etapes.justification: It ties the answer back to the question.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A clean river protects health and the life of the whole town.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
(a) Water pollution is the addition of harmful substances, such as waste, sewage or chemicals, to rivers, lakes or the sea, so that the water becomes unsafe for people, animals and plants.

(b) First, the town council and residents can dispose of waste properly by using bins and regular refuse collection, so that rubbish is not thrown into the river. Second, sewage and the waste of factories and workshops can be treated before they reach the water, which removes germs and poisonous substances. Third, the town can organise education campaigns and apply fines to those who dump waste in the river, which changes behaviour. In this way the river stays safe for drinking, fishing and washing, and the health of the town is protected.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Pollution means any dirt or litter lying around.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Litter is only one source of pollution. Pollution is the release of substances or energy that cause harm, including smoke, sewage, chemicals and noise.
items.correction_markdown: Pollution is the release of harmful substances or energy into the air, water or soil, which harms people, animals and plants.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Conservation means that resources must never be touched.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Conservation allows use, but a careful and planned use that leaves enough for the future.
items.correction_markdown: Conservation is the wise use, protection and management of resources so that they last for future generations.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Afforestation is the cutting of trees.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The two words are opposites. Cutting forests is deforestation, while afforestation is planting trees.
items.correction_markdown: Afforestation means planting trees; deforestation means clearing forests without replacing them.

items.erreur_markdown: Asked for the effects of pollution, a student lists 'burning rubbish, dumping sewage, using chemicals'.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are causes, the actions that start the problem, not the results that follow.
items.correction_markdown: Give effects such as diseases, death of fish, acid rain and poor harvests, and explain each one.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Noise is not a kind of pollution because it cannot be seen.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Pollution does not have to be visible. Loud and constant sound harms hearing and health.
items.correction_markdown: Noise pollution is unwanted loud sound that harms people's health and comfort.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the kind of pollution shown in each case: (a) exhaust fumes from old taxis in a crowded street; (b) untreated sewage flowing into a stream; (c) a generator running loudly all night next to houses; (d) plastic bags buried in a vegetable garden.

A community forest has 2,000 trees. Loggers cut 15% of them, and the community plants 150 new trees. (a) How many trees were cut? (b) How many trees are in the forest after the planting? (c) Is the forest still suffering deforestation? Explain.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 15% of 2,000 = 15 / 100 x 2,000 = **300 trees**.

(b) Trees left = 2,000 - 300 = 1,700. After planting: 1,700 + 150 = **1,850 trees**.

(c) Yes, the forest still loses trees, because 1,850 is less than 2,000 (a net loss of 150 trees). The planting reduces the damage, but to conserve the forest the community must plant at least as many trees as are cut, and protect the young trees.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss how environmental degradation can make poverty worse in a rural area, and propose three measures that the community and the State can take to conserve the environment.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for a developed discussion and three explained measures.

Discussion: when forests are cleared and soil is eroded, farms give smaller harvests, so families earn less and may cut even more trees for money, which deepens the damage. Polluted streams cause diseases, so money is spent on treatment and children miss school. Loss of wildlife and fish reduces food and income.

Measures: (1) The State can make and enforce laws against illegal logging and dumping. (2) The community can plant trees and protect water sources. (3) Schools and local radio can educate people on waste management and cleaner farming. Other valid measures: recycling, cleaner energy, proper sewage systems.

**Degradation lowers incomes and health, and conservation protects both.**

items_markdown: Environmental degradation is the damage and wearing out of the environment; conservation is the wise use and protection of resources for the future.
Pollution is the release of harmful substances or energy into air, water or soil; the main kinds are air, water, soil and noise pollution.
Deforestation is clearing forests without replacing them; afforestation and reforestation are planting trees.
Causes, effects and remedies must be kept separate and each point explained in a sentence.
Remedies include laws, education, tree planting, waste management, treatment of sewage and cleaner energy.
World Environment Day is on 5 June.
